text_en: This “King Melchizedek of Salem, priest of the Most High God, met Abraham as he was returning from defeating the kings and blessed him”;
text_cn: 原来这默基瑟德是撒冷王，是至高者天主的司祭；当亚巴郎打败众王回来时，他来迎接，且祝福了他。

text_en: and to him Abraham apportioned “one-tenth of everything. ” His name, in the first place, means “king of righteousness”; next he is also king of Salem, that is, “king of peace. ”
text_cn: 亚巴郎就由所有的一切之中，拿出十分之一分给了他；他的名字默基瑟德，第一可称作“正义之王”，他也可称作“撒冷之王”，就是“和平之王”之意。

text_en: Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.
text_cn: 他无父，无母，无族谱，生无始，寿无终：他好像天主子，永久身为司祭。

text_en: See how great he is! Even Abraham the patriarch gave him a tenth of the spoils.
text_cn: 你们要想想：这人是多么伟大，连圣祖亚巴郎也由上等的战利品中，取了十分之一献给了他！

text_en: And those descendants of Levi who receive the priestly office have a commandment in the law to collect tithes from the people, that is, from their kindred, though these also are descended from Abraham.
text_cn: 那些由肋未子孙中领受司祭职的，固然有命向人民，按法律征收什一之物，即向他们的弟兄，虽然都是出自亚巴郎的腰中；

text_en: But this man, who does not belong to their ancestry, collected tithes from Abraham and blessed him who had received the promises.
text_cn: 可是不属于他们世系的那一位，却收了亚巴郎的什一之物，并祝福了那蒙受恩许的。

text_en: It is beyond dispute that the inferior is blessed by the superior.
text_cn: 从来，在下的受在上的祝福，这是无人可反对的。

text_en: In the one case, tithes are received by those who are mortal; in the other, by one of whom it is testified that he lives.
text_cn: 在这里那些领受什一之物的，是有死的人；但在那里领受什一之物的，却是一位证明了常活着的人。

text_en: One might even say that Levi himself, who receives tithes, paid tithes through Abraham,
text_cn: 并且可说：连那领受什一之物的肋未，也藉着亚巴郎交纳了什一之物，

text_en: for he was still in the loins of his ancestor when Melchizedek met him.
text_cn: 因为当默基瑟德迎接亚巴郎的时候，肋未还在祖先的腰中。

text_en: Now if perfection had been attainable through the levitical priesthood—for the people received the law under this priesthood—what further need would there have been to speak of another priest arising according to the order of Melchizedek, rather than one according to the order of Aaron?
text_cn: 那么，如果藉着肋未司祭职能有成全──因为选民就是本着这司祭职接受了法律──为什么还需要兴起另一位，按照默基瑟德品位的司祭，而不称为按照亚郎的品位呢？

text_en: For when there is a change in the priesthood, there is necessarily a change in the law as well.
text_cn: 如今司祭职一变更，法律也必然变更，

text_en: Now the one of whom these things are spoken belonged to another tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.
text_cn: 因为这里所论到的那一位，原是属于另一支派，由这一支派中，没有一个人曾在祭坛前服务过。

text_en: For it is evident that our Lord was descended from Judah, and in connection with that tribe Moses said nothing about priests.
text_cn: 显然我们的主是由犹大支派出生的，关于这一支派，梅瑟从未提到司祭的事。

text_en: It is even more obvious when another priest arises, resembling Melchizedek,
text_cn: 既然有另一位司祭，是按照默基瑟德的品级兴起的，那么我们所讨论的就更显明了，

text_en: one who has become a priest, not through a legal requirement concerning physical descent, but through the power of an indestructible life.
text_cn: 因为他之成为司祭，并不是按照血统所规定的法则，而是按照不可消灭的生命的德能，

text_en: For it is attested of him, “You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek. ”
text_cn: 因为有圣经给他作证：“你照默基瑟德的品位永做司祭。”

text_en: There is, on the one hand, the abrogation of an earlier commandment because it was weak and ineffectual
text_cn: 先前的诫命之废除，是由于它的弱点和无用，

text_en: (for the law made nothing perfect); there is, on the other hand, the introduction of a better hope, through which we approach God.
text_cn: 因为法律本来就不能成就什么；可是如今引进了一个更好的希望，因着这希望，我们才能亲近天主。

text_en: This was confirmed with an oath; for others who became priests took their office without an oath,
text_cn: 再者，耶稣成为司祭，是具有天主誓言的，其他的司祭并没有这种誓言就成了司祭。

text_en: but this one became a priest with an oath, because of the one who said to him, “The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind, ‘You are a priest forever’”—
text_cn: 耶稣成为司祭，却具有誓言，因为天主向他说：“上主一发了誓，他决不再反悔；你永为司祭。”

text_en: accordingly Jesus has also become the guarantee of a better covenant.
text_cn: 如此，耶稣就成了更好的盟约的担保人。

text_en: Furthermore, the former priests were many in number, because they were prevented by death from continuing in office;
text_cn: 再者，肋未人成为司祭的，人数众多，因为死亡阻碍他们长久留任，

text_en: but he holds his priesthood permanently, because he continues forever.
text_cn: 但是耶稣因永远长存，具有不可消逝的司祭品位。

text_en: Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
text_cn: 因此，凡由他而接近天主的人，他全能拯救，因为他常活着，为他们转求。

text_en: For it was fitting that we should have such a high priest, holy, blameless, undefiled, separated from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
text_cn: 这样的大司祭才适合于我们，他是圣善的、无辜的、无玷的、别于罪人的、高于诸天的；

text_en: Unlike the other high priests, he has no need to offer sacrifices day after day, first for his own sins, and then for those of the people; this he did once for all when he offered himself.
text_cn: 他无须像那些大司祭一样，每日要先为自己的罪，后为人民的罪祭献牺牲；因为他奉献了自己，只一次而永远完成了这事，

text_en: For the law appoints as high priests those who are subject to weakness, but the word of the oath, which came later than the law, appoints a Son who has been made perfect forever.
text_cn: 因为法律所立为大司祭的人是有弱点的；可是在法律以后，以誓言所立的圣子，却是成全的，直到永远。
